item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-bc81f6398e7b90c3","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"An IAEA follow-up review of Laguna Verde reported improvements in ageing management, training, and data management after recommendations from a 2019 mission, while identifying remaining work on a comprehensive periodic safety review and full electrical-equipment qualification; Mexico's operator and regulator received the findings and expressed continued cooperation.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.4","1B.7","1B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Contextual evidence from 2022 relevant to the nuclear-safety posture inherited and carried into 2023; the document does not attribute the actions directly to López Obrador.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution to López Obrador; actions are attributed to CFE, CNSNS, and the IAEA process.","limitations":["The source reports plant-level safety actions, not presidential decisions, funding, enforcement, or end-2023 resolution of remaining findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-455aa431451b04dd","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A February 2023 report stated that an investigation identified at least eleven Pemex contracts with Baker Hughes and affiliates from 2019 to 2021, exceeding $29 million, including contracts signed after AMLO's son José Ramón López Beltrán occupied a residence owned by a Baker Hughes executive; the report said the findings contradicted earlier denials of a conflict of interest.","question_ids":["5B.5","7B.1","7B.2","7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Reported in 2023 and concerning contracts from 2019–2021; relevant to accountability and integrity during the 2023 presidency but not proof of a final legal finding.","ruler_attribution":"The report concerns López Obrador's son and Pemex, and reports that López Obrador denied a conflict of interest; it does not establish that López Obrador personally directed or benefited from the contracts.","limitations":["The source is a journalistic report summarizing an investigation, not a court or audit determination; alleged conflict of interest is not equivalent to proven corruption or personal enrichment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1e63e7c17aa1be98","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The ASF characterized irregularities totaling 12.3 billion pesos in Segalmex maize and bean contracts from 2019 to 2021 as an emblematic diversion case; under director Leonel Cota Montaño, 1,000 staff were assigned to cooperate with the ASF, enabling findings of a probable 2.436 billion pesos diverted in 2021 in addition to nearly 10 billion from 2019–2020, and 65 criminal complaints were filed.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","6B.5","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","8B.3","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly reported in March 2023, with underlying irregularities spanning 2019–2021.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes corrective cooperation to Segalmex director Leonel Cota Montaño and reports ASF oversight; it does not establish López Obrador's personal responsibility for the diversion.","limitations":["The report describes probable diversion and administrative responses, not final adjudication, recovery, or presidential personal involvement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f3dc478c49c623ce","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In his September 2023 fifth-government report, López Obrador defended the armed forces' expanded public roles and denied that this constituted militarization; he asserted that repression, massacres, torture, disappearances, and human-rights violations were not occurring, and claimed reductions in federal crime, homicide, feminicide, vehicle theft, and kidnapping, alongside a 128,000-member National Guard and extensive military involvement in security, infrastructure, logistics, and public services.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","4B.2","4B.5","6B.1","6B.2","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct presidential statements and reported government activities in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributed to López Obrador's fifth-government report and his described delegation of roles to Sedena, Semar, and the National Guard.","limitations":["The document reports presidential claims and listed activities, but does not independently verify the crime reductions, human-rights assertions, implementation quality, or civilian oversight."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e44098557d2c0acc","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Artículo 19 documented 272 press-related aggressions in Mexico during the first half of 2023, including intimidation, harassment, illegitimate use of public power, and threats; it reported that 47 of 61 illegitimate-use cases involved stigmatization, that violence and impunity persisted, and that three journalists were possibly murdered because of their work while one was disappeared during the period.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.4","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Direct evidence concerning January–June 2023, with the article published in September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report situates the figures within López Obrador's administration and attributes concerns to stigmatizing discourse by public officials and impunity; it does not establish that López Obrador personally ordered individual attacks.","limitations":["The figures are documented incidents and reported organizational findings; the source does not establish presidential causation for each aggression or assess all protective measures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4a28258b3a0b1d13","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"A study of more than 1.5 million Mexican public contracts from 2013–2020 found that after the 2018 government transition, spending with companies later identified as corrupt decreased substantially, but many contracting patterns persisted and some changes suggested increased corruption risk.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","7B.9","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Contextual evidence covering 2013–2020, not direct evidence for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The study compares administrations and reports effects following the 2018 transition, but does not attribute individual contracting decisions or outcomes directly to López Obrador.","limitations":["The study ends in 2020 and uses companies later identified as corrupt; it does not measure 2023 performance or establish personal presidential intent."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3a33587cb3269f19","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"A 2022 study proposed a machine-learning ensemble model for identifying potentially corrupt Mexican public-procurement contracts and found that buyer–supplier relationship variables were more important predictors than individual-contract features.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.6","7B.9","8B.8"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Methodological context from 2022; the abstract does not report a 2023 government action or outcome.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution to López Obrador or his administration.","limitations":["The document presents a detection tool and does not identify specific 2023 contracts, officials, enforcement actions, or presidential conduct."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1e4cff1120d66afa","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"A 2023 study applied ownership, management, and contracting data to two documented Mexican procurement-corruption cases, identifying connected shell-company networks, quantifying impacts and favoritism, and arguing for prevention measures and legal reform.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.6","7B.9","8B.8"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Published in 2023 but based on documented cases and analytical data not specified in the abstract as occurring during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution to López Obrador or his administration.","limitations":["The abstract does not identify the cases, responsible officials, presidential actions, or 2023 enforcement outcomes."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-8b90a137d973d3e4","SRC-977194f621c4678e","SRC-abf8888683dbf163","SRC-5ff54ba512cd4a31"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied AI documents describe catastrophic and generative-AI risks or proposed regulation but contain no fact about López Obrador, Mexico, or his 2023 decisions.","Several procurement studies provide contextual or methodological evidence rather than direct 2023 evidence of presidential conduct.","No supplied document materially addresses López Obrador's conduct for most nuclear-risk, international-peace, electoral, social-welfare, or succession questions."]}
